accipiter-cooperii.note: Slim hawk: slate-blue back, dark cap, red-orange eye, rusty-barred breast, long rounded tail with broad dark bands and a white tip.

actitis-macularius.note: Adult breeding Spotted Sandpiper: brown-olive upperparts, white underparts boldly spotted with round black spots, a white eye-stripe, a dark line through the eye, a pink-orange bill with a dark tip, and yellowish-pink legs. Short tail, horizontal stance. Not a Solitary Sandpiper (no breast spots, white eye-ring).

anas-crecca.note: Adult male: chestnut head with a broad iridescent green eye patch edged in cream, grey body with fine barring, a vertical white shoulder stripe, a creamy patch at the tail and a black rump. Small dabbling duck with a small dark bill.

antigone-canadensis.note: Tall grey crane with a long neck and legs, a bare red patch on the forehead and crown, a pale cheek, a long straight dark bill, and a bustle of drooping feathers over the tail. Not a Great Blue Heron.

archilochus-colubris.note: Adult male Ruby-throated Hummingbird -- TINY, about 9 cm: a compact, round-bodied bird with a big head, a very short tail and short wings whose tips nearly reach the tail tip; perches upright with tiny, barely visible feet. Long straight needle bill as long as the head; metallic emerald-green back and crown; glittering ruby-red throat; greyish-white underparts with greenish flanks; dark, slightly forked tail. Never swallow- or thrush-like in shape.

ardea-herodias.note: Great Blue Heron, not the Eurasian Grey Heron: a muted slate blue-grey body (grey, not blue-teal), neck washed pale greyish-buff to lavender-grey, rich chestnut-rufous thighs and a rufous bend of the wing, black-and-white streaked foreneck, white face and crown centre with a broad black stripe ending in plumes, long yellowish dagger bill, shaggy grey breast plumes. Very tall with a long S-curved neck.

bombycilla-cedrorum.note: Sleek, crested, silky plumage: warm brown-tan head, crest and breast fading to a pale yellow belly; grey wings, rump and tail; a narrow black mask through the eye, edged with fine white, and a black chin; bright yellow band across the tail tip; small waxy red tips on the secondaries.

branta-canadensis.note: Black head and long black neck with a white 'chinstrap' patch, grey-brown body, paler breast, white undertail, black tail and legs.

buteo-jamaicensis.note: Stocky, broad-winged hawk: brown back, pale breast with a band of dark streaks across the belly, brick-red tail.

buteo-lineatus.note: Rufous-orange barred breast, reddish shoulders, black-and-white checkered flight feathers, black tail with narrow white bands.

calidris-minutilla.note: Tiny sandpiper: dark streaky brown back with pale feather edges, streaked brown breast, white belly, thin slightly downcurved bill, and yellowish-green legs. Smaller than the Semipalmated Sandpiper.

canis-latrans.note: Grizzled grey-tan coat, rusty legs and ears, narrow muzzle, bushy black-tipped tail carried low.

cardinalis-cardinalis.note: Adult male: red all over, underparts included -- no pale or buff belly, only a slightly softer red below. Thick, conical, bright coral-red bill (never black or dark), set in a black face mask that surrounds the bill base and covers the throat. Tall pointed red crest; wings and tail a deeper, duller red.

catharus-guttatus.note: Brown back with a contrasting rufous tail, thin white eye-ring, spotted breast. Not Swainson's Thrush.

catharus-ustulatus.note: Olive-brown back and tail all one color, bold buffy spectacles around the eye, buff-washed spotted breast. Not Hermit Thrush.

certhia-americana.note: Small, slim, brown bark-creeper: streaked brown and buff back, white underparts, a long thin downcurved bill, a pale eyebrow stripe, and a long stiff tail braced against the bark. Clings to a trunk, never perches crosswise.

chaetura-pelagica.note: Chimney Swift shown at rest clinging upright to a vertical surface, never perched crosswise on a twig: a small cigar-shaped sooty grey-brown bird with a short, stubby tail whose spiny tail tips brace against the surface; very long, narrow, pointed wingtips cross and extend past the tail; short, wide, flat head with a tiny bill; pale grey throat.

coccyzus-americanus.note: Slender, long-tailed cuckoo: grey-brown upperparts, white underparts, a long decurved bill with a yellow lower mandible, a yellow eye-ring, rufous patches in the primaries, and a long tail with large white spots on the underside. Not a Black-billed Cuckoo (which has an all-dark bill).

colaptes-auratus.note: Yellow-shafted (eastern) adult male: grey crown and nape with a red crescent on the back of the nape, tan-buff face, black moustache stripe from the bill; bold black crescent bib; buff-white underparts with round black spots; brown back and wings finely barred black; white rump; yellow shafts and undersides to the flight and tail feathers.

contopus-virens.note: Small, plain flycatcher: dark olive-grey above, pale grey-olive breast and flanks, whitish throat and belly, two thin pale wing bars, a peaked head, a bill with a pale yellow base to the lower mandible, and very long wings that reach well down the tail. No eye ring.

corthylio-calendula.note: Tiny, plain olive with a broken white eye-ring and a white wing bar; the male's red crown patch shows only as a small flash.

corvus-brachyrhynchos.note: All glossy black including bill, legs and feet, with a thick straight bill, bristly feathers at the base of the bill and a square-ended tail. Not a Common Grackle.

dryobates-pubescens.note: Tiny bill, much shorter than the head; white outer tail feathers barred with black. Male has a small red nape patch. Not Hairy Woodpecker.

dryobates-villosus.note: Long chisel bill, nearly as long as the head; a broad, unbroken white stripe running down the centre of the black back, clearly visible; black wings with rows of white spots; plain white outer tail feathers; bold black-and-white striped face. Male has a small red nape patch. Not Downy Woodpecker.

dryocopus-pileatus.note: Crow-sized woodpecker: mostly black body with a flaming red pointed crest, a white stripe running down the neck, a black stripe through the eye, and a long chisel bill. Adult male has a red stripe from the bill base.

dumetella-carolinensis.note: Slender, uniform slate-grey bird with a neat black cap, a long dark tail, chestnut-rusty undertail coverts, a thin dark bill and dark eye. No wing bars or eye-ring; not a mockingbird (no white wing patches).

empidonax-virescens.note: Small olive-grey flycatcher: olive-green back and crown, pale whitish throat, white or pale-yellow belly with a faint olive wash on the breast, two bold whitish wing bars, a conspicuous whitish eye-ring, a fairly large flat head and a long, broad pinkish-orange lower bill. Not a Willow Flycatcher (no eye-ring, browner) or a vireo.

falco-sparverius.note: Adult male American Kestrel: small falcon with blue-grey wings and crown topped with a rufous cap, two bold black vertical facial stripes on a white face, rufous back and tail barred in black with a broad black band near a white tip, cream-buff underparts spotted with black, and a short hooked grey bill. Not a Merlin (no facial stripes).

haemorhous-mexicanus.note: Adult male: rosy red forehead, eyebrow, throat, breast and rump; brown cap and brown cheek patch; buff-white belly and flanks with bold blurry brown streaks; streaked brown back and wings with thin pale wing bars. Short, stubby, curved grey bill. Not Purple Finch: no rosy wash on the back or wings.

haliaeetus-leucocephalus.note: Adult: pure white head, neck and tail, dark chocolate-brown body and wings with paler feather edges, massive hooked bright yellow bill, yellow eye and yellow, unfeathered legs. Large and long-winged; not a Golden Eagle or a juvenile (which is mottled brown and white).

hirundo-rustica.note: Adult male Barn Swallow: glossy steel-blue upperparts, rusty-orange forehead and throat, a blue-black breast band, cinnamon-buff underparts, and a long, deeply forked tail with very long thin outer streamers. Pointed wings that reach to the tail base; small short bill; tiny feet.

hydroprogne-caspia.note: Very large, heavy tern: thick blood-red bill with a dark tip, black cap, pale grey back, dark undersides to the wingtips.

junco-hyemalis.note: Slate-coloured (eastern) male: hood, back, wings and breast a uniform neutral charcoal grey -- no blue, teal or brown tint anywhere -- ending in a clean line against a pure white belly; pale pinkish conical bill; white outer tail feathers; no wing bars or streaks.

larus-delawarensis.note: Yellow bill with a black ring near the tip, yellow legs, pale grey back, black wingtips with white spots.

leiothlypis-peregrina.note: Small plain warbler: olive-green back, clean pale grey head, a thin dark line through the eye, a whitish eyebrow stripe, and white to pale yellow-white underparts. No wing bars, no streaks.

megaceryle-alcyon.note: Adult male: large shaggy crested head, blue-grey crest, back and breast band, white collar, white belly, long thick dagger bill, short tail. The male lacks the rusty belly band of the female.

melanerpes-carolinus.note: Black-and-white barred back, pale buff face and breast, red cap and nape on the male; the belly has only a faint reddish wash. Not Red-headed Woodpecker.

melanerpes-erythrocephalus.note: Entire head and neck solid crimson, solid black back, large white patches on the rear of the wing, white belly.

meleagris-gallopavo.note: Adult male (tom): very large, dark bronzy-black body with iridescent copper and green sheen, bare reddish-pink to blue-white head and neck with warty skin, a red wattle and snood, long pinkish legs, and a broad rounded tail banded in chestnut and black. Closed tail, carried low; not a fanned strutting display and not a domestic turkey.

molothrus-ater.note: Male: glossy black body with a brown head, short conical finch-like bill.

myiarchus-crinitus.note: Large flycatcher: olive-brown back, slight bushy crest, grey throat and breast, bright lemon-yellow belly, rufous edges to the wings and tail, and two pale wing bars.

pandion-haliaetus.note: Large raptor with a dark brown back, white underparts, a white head with a broad dark brown stripe through the eye, a hooked dark bill, and pale yellow-grey legs; may show a faint necklace of brown streaks on the breast.

passer-domesticus.note: Breeding male: grey crown, chestnut-brown band from the eye back around the nape, pale grey-white cheeks, black bib on the throat and upper breast, black between bill and eye; streaked chestnut, black and buff back; one white wing bar; plain pale grey underparts; stout conical black bill.

pheucticus-ludovicianus.note: Adult male: black head, back and wings with white wing patches and a white rump; white belly; a triangular rose-red patch on the breast; a thick, pale conical bill.

piranga-rubra.note: Adult male Summer Tanager: bright, saturated strawberry-red all over (never pink, rose or dull), wings only slightly darker red; thick, pale yellowish-horn bill; no crest and no black mask. Not a Northern Cardinal or Scarlet Tanager.

poecile-atricapillus.note: Black cap and bib, white cheeks, bold white edges on the wing feathers, buff flanks. Not Carolina Chickadee.

poecile-carolinensis.note: Black cap and neat black bib, white cheeks, grey wings with little white edging, pale grey-buff flanks. Not Black-capped Chickadee.

progne-subis.note: Adult male Purple Martin: entirely glossy dark blue-black with a deep violet-purple sheen -- never green or teal -- including the belly; blackish-brown wings and tail; a large, sturdy swallow with long pointed wings crossing over a slightly forked tail at rest, and a short, stout black bill.

quiscalus-quiscula.note: Adult male: long keel-shaped tail, long dark bill, pale yellow eye; glossy iridescent purple-blue head and breast with bronzy-brown body. Not a crow (much slimmer, with a long tail).

regulus-satrapa.note: Tiny: black-and-white striped face with a yellow crown stripe bordered in black (orange center in males).

sayornis-phoebe.note: Eastern Phoebe: dark blackish-brown head, olive-grey-brown back, dingy white throat and underparts with a faint yellow wash on the belly, plain wings without bold wing bars, no eye-ring, a small black bill and a longish dark tail. Upright, round-headed flycatcher. Not an Eastern Wood-Pewee (which has wing bars).

sciurus-carolinensis.note: Grey coat with a brownish wash, white belly, large bushy grey tail fringed with white.

setophaga-coronata.note: Adult male (breeding, eastern 'Myrtle'): blue-grey back streaked with black, white throat, black streaked breast, and bright yellow patches on the crown, each side of the breast and the rump; white wing bars and white tail spots.

setophaga-magnolia.note: Adult male (breeding): grey crown and black mask, white eyebrow stripe, yellow throat and belly with bold black streaks, black back, large white patch on the wing, and a black tail with white band partway down.

setophaga-palmarum.note: Small warbler that bobs its tail: olive-brown back, rusty-chestnut cap in breeding plumage, yellow eyebrow stripe, streaked yellow breast and belly, and bright yellow undertail. No wing bars.

setophaga-virens.note: Adult male: olive-green back and crown, bright yellow face, black throat and bib that runs into black streaks along the flanks, white belly, two white wing bars.

sialia-sialis.note: Adult male: deep blue head, back, wings and tail; rusty-orange throat and breast; white belly and undertail. Not Mountain Bluebird (no orange) or Indigo Bunting.

sitta-canadensis.note: Small nuthatch: blue-grey back, rusty-orange underparts, black cap, a bold white eyebrow stripe and a black stripe through the eye, a short tail, and a thin sharp bill. Smaller and rustier than the White-breasted Nuthatch.

sitta-carolinensis.note: Adult male: clean white face, throat and breast -- no peach or buff there, a faint grey wash at most; glossy black cap and nape; blue-grey back and wings with black-and-white tertials; chestnut undertail coverts; short blue-grey tail with black and white corners. Long, straight, slender grey bill with a slightly upturned tip. Black eye sits in the white face with no eye line. Compact and big-headed with almost no neck. Not Red-breasted Nuthatch.

sphyrapicus-varius.note: Adult male: red forehead and crown, red throat bordered by black and white face stripes, black bib, pale yellow wash on the belly, black-and-white barred back, and a long white stripe along the folded wing. Not a Downy Woodpecker.

spinus-pinus.note: Heavily brown-streaked all over, thin sharply pointed bill, yellow flashes in the wing and tail.

spinus-tristis.note: Breeding male: brilliant lemon-yellow body, underparts included -- no peach or buff wash; only the undertail coverts are white. Neat black cap on the forehead only, wings jet black throughout -- in flight, show the bird from slightly above so the black upper surfaces of BOTH wings face the viewer, never a pale or grey underwing -- with bold white wing bars and white feather edges, black tail with white inner webs. Small conical pinkish-orange bill.

spizella-pusilla.note: Small slim sparrow: grey face, rusty cap and eye line, a pink bill, a white eye-ring, a plain buff-grey breast with no streaks or breast spot, two white wing bars, and a long notched tail.

streptopelia-decaocto.note: Pale pinkish-grey dove: sandy buff-grey body, a thin black half-collar edged in white on the back of the neck, red eye, dark primaries, and a long square tail with a pale tip. Larger and paler than a Mourning Dove, with a squared (not pointed) tail and no black spots on the wing.

strix-varia.note: Large round-headed owl with no ear tufts: dark brown eyes, grey-brown plumage barred horizontally on the upper breast and streaked vertically on the belly, a pale facial disc, and a yellow bill. Not a Great Horned Owl.

sturnella-magna.note: Adult Eastern Meadowlark: bright yellow throat and breast with a bold black V across the breast, brown-streaked buff-white upperparts, a striped crown with a yellow spot before the eye, long pointed bill, short tail with white outer feathers, and long pinkish legs. Stocky and short-tailed, standing upright.

tamias-striatus.note: Small ground squirrel: bold black and white stripes down the back and across the face, rusty rump, short furred tail.

thryothorus-ludovicianus.note: Plump rich rusty-brown wren with a long bold white eyebrow stripe, buffy-orange underparts, white throat, fine dark barring on wings and tail, a slightly downcurved bill, and a short tail often cocked up.

tringa-flavipes.note: Bright yellow legs; thin, straight bill about as long as the head. Not Greater Yellowlegs.

tringa-melanoleuca.note: Bright yellow legs; bill clearly longer than the head and slightly upturned. Not Lesser Yellowlegs.

troglodytes-aedon.note: Small plain brown wren: unstreaked greyish-brown above with fine dark barring on wings and tail, pale grey-buff underparts, a faint pale eye ring, a thin slightly downcurved bill, and a short tail often cocked up. No bold eyebrow stripe (not Carolina Wren).

turdus-migratorius.note: Adult male: blackish head with broken white eye-arcs, yellow bill, white-streaked throat; deep brick-orange breast and flanks; dark grey-brown back, wings and tail; white lower belly and undertail. A large, upright thrush.

tyrannus-tyrannus.note: Black head, black-grey back, white underparts, a broad white tip to the black tail, and a small hidden red crown patch.

vireo-flavifrons.note: Adult Yellow-throated Vireo (reference is an old, yellowed printed plate -- use true living colours): bright lemon-yellow throat and breast and bold yellow 'spectacles' (eye-ring joined to the bill); olive-green head and back fading to a grey rump; clean white belly and undertail; dark grey wings with two bold white wing bars; dark eye; stout, slightly hooked grey bill. Not a Pine Warbler (no streaks, thicker bill).

zenaida-macroura.note: Plump, small-headed dove: soft grey-brown upperparts, pinkish-buff head and breast, a small black spot below the ear, a few black spots on the folded wing; long pointed tail with white-edged outer feathers; thin dark bill; pinkish-red legs; pale blue eye-ring.

zonotrichia-albicollis.note: Crisp white throat patch, yellow spot in front of the eye, black-and-white crown stripes, dark bill.

zonotrichia-leucophrys.note: Bold black-and-white crown stripes, pink-orange bill, plain grey breast; no white throat patch and no yellow before the eye.
